pr_title: [PVR] EPG persistence speed improvements and fixes

issue_context.title: Long shutdown time and intensive HDD usage updating EPG for large IPTV playlists
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug

Kodi creates and deletes the `Epg*.db-journal` for every EPG item being persisted. This causes excessive HDD wear and long shutdown times (2-5 minutes) if IPTV playlist and EPG have several thousands of live TV channels and VODs.

### Expected Behavior

The journal files for `Epg*.db` should be processed in memory so shutdown times are instant (~5-8 seconds on the same playlist / EPG pair vs the unmodified setup)

### Actual Behavior

The iotop graph is shown below:

![iotop-excessive-hdd-usage](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3913291/80948267-67bcfa80-8dfa-11ea-9dc6-453407414c3c.png)

The shutdown time is very long (2-5 minutes on AMD E-300 dual-core CPU and 5400rpm HDD)

### Possible Fix

I created the script and the systemd unit mounting the `$KODIPROFILE/userdata/Database` as an overlayfs with the lower directory of original `Database` directory and `tmpfs` mount as upper-directory:

[kodi-mount-overlay.sh](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/4573561/kodi-mount-overlay.sh.txt)
[kodi-mount-overlay.service](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/4573566/kodi-mount-overlay.service.txt)

With this ugly hack, the shutdown time and disk usage is desirable.

### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Generate the test playlist / EPG pair using the script:
[generate-big-test-m3u-epg.sh](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/4573573/generate-big-test-m3u-epg.sh.txt)

2. Load the M3U and EPG into IPTV Simple Client and let Kodi process the channels and EPG markers
3. Exit Kodi and observe high disk usage running `sudio iotop` and lots of created-and-vanishing `Epg36.db-journal` in `$KODIPROFILE/userdata/Database`

### Debuglog

The debuglog can be found here:

[kodi.log](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/files/4573629/kodi.log)

The log ended after I had to issue
``` shell
kill -9 $(pidof kodi-x11)
```

on my test VM.

### Your Environment
Used Operating system:

 - [ ] Android
 - [ ] iOS
 - [x] Linux
 - [ ] OSX
 - [ ] Raspberry-Pi
 - [ ] Windows
 - [ ] Windows UWP

 - Operating system version/name: Debian 10 buster amd64
 - Kodi version: 19.0 trunk

Another reason you have so short times is SSD drive. SSD drives have random access speed ~10x higher than the best HDD hence the speedup. Also, OSX might be contributing to filesystem caching speed as well.

I will set up a test but I am pretty sure for PVR it is not a good idea not only for speed because the delayed writes could in theory write bad data.   The issue of harmonizing EPG update settings is significant too.

client 1 reads epg
client 2 reads new epg
client 2 exits and writes data immediately
client 1 writes potentially stale data over a period of time.

Fortunately based on direct access speed the patch could greatly reduce the risk of issues and collisions, but not settings differences.
